answer.rationale: The write-path p99 is climbing during peak settlement traffic. The most recent relevant learned lever (memory_b5) shows that routing reporting/dashboard read queries to read replicas removed load from the primary and let write latency recover the same day. This is a narrow, reversible, low-blast-radius intervention that directly reduces load on the saturated write path without touching the security-critical release (memory_b1 is noted but the compliance constraint makes rollback non-viable), and without the latency/complexity of regional failover during peak writes. Circuit breakers (memory_b4) protected against partner outage dependency failures; that is not the current failure mode. Adding capacity would help but is slower to land and less targeted than offloading reads first. Requesting verification of memory_b5 to confirm the replica-routing details and guardrails, and memory_b3 to confirm provisioning headroom patterns in case capacity add becomes the next-window follow-up.
